title: Lesson 23: Extending the concept of fractions. Equal fractions

exercises.text: A __________ is written in the form ab where a and b are integers and b0.
In the expression ab, the top part a is called the __________, while the bottom part b represents the total equal parts divided.
The bottom number b in any fraction ab is known as the __________ and must never equal zero.
When two different-looking fractions represent the exact same value, such as 12 and 24, they are called __________.
According to the __________, multiplying or dividing both the top and bottom numbers of a fraction by the same non-zero integer gives an equal value.
The process of __________ involves dividing both parts of a fraction by a common divisor to make the numbers smaller.
When a fraction cannot be reduced any further because its numerator and denominator have no common divisors other than 1 and -1, it is called an __________.

title: Lesson 24: Comparing fractions. Positive mixed numbers

exercises.text: Before adding fractions with different bottom numbers, we must start by __________ so that they share the same bottom value.
Any number like 12 or 24 that is divisible by both 3 and 4 is called a __________ of those two numbers.
The __________ of 4 and 6 is 12, because 12 is the smallest positive number that both 4 and 6 divide into evenly.
To rewrite 12 and 13 as 36 and 26, we use 6 as the __________.
Choosing the __________ makes calculations much simpler because it keeps the numbers as small as possible.
__________ with the same positive denominator is straightforward: the one with the larger numerator is greater.
A __________ combines a whole number and a proper fraction into a single value, such as 325.
When we rewrite the improper fraction 73 as 213, we create a __________.
In the expression 213, the number 2 represents the __________.
In the same expression 213, the 13 that is smaller than 1 is known as the __________.

title: Lesson 25: Addition and subtraction of fractions
wordBank: Adding fractions with the same denominator

exercises.text: __________ is very straightforward: you simply add the numerators together and keep the bottom number unchanged.
answers: Adding fractions with the same denominator

exercises.text: When __________ like 13 and 14, you must first rewrite them with a common positive denominator before combining their numerators.
The __________ of 35 is -35, because adding these two values together gives a sum of 0.
__________ works just like addition: if they share the same bottom number, you subtract the second numerator from the first and keep the denominator.
Thanks to the __________, swapping the order of two fractions in an addition problem, such as 12+23=23+12, does not change the final result.
Using the __________ allows us to group fractions differently when adding three or more numbers, making it easier to pair fractions with matching denominators first.

title: Lesson 26: Multiplication and division of fractions

exercises.text: __________ does not require a common denominator; you simply multiply the numerators together and multiply the denominators together.
Flipping 34 upside down gives 43, which is called the __________ of the original fraction.
When performing __________, you keep the first fraction the same and multiply it by the flipped version of the second fraction.

title: Lesson 27: Two problems on fractions
wordBank: Finding a number from its fraction

exercises.text: To calculate a __________, such as finding 54 of 120, we multiply the given value 120 by 54 to get 150.
__________ requires dividing the known part by the given fraction; for example, if 34 of an unknown amount is 180, we divide 180 by 34 to get 240.
answers: Finding a number from its fraction

exercises.text: A fraction whose denominator is a power of 10, such as 1710 or -34100, is called a __________.
Any value like -1.7 or -0.025 that is less than zero is known as a __________.
Numbers greater than zero, such as 5.1 or 12.3, are examples of a __________.
Both negative and positive values written with a comma belong to the category of a __________.
In the number 215.417, the __________ is the dot that separates the digits on the left from the digits on the right.
Looking at 215.417, the digits 215 to the left of the separator form the __________.
In the same number 215.417, the digits 417 to the right of the separator make up the __________.
The __________ of 3.15 is -3.15, because they are opposites on the number line.
When __________ that are both negative, the one with the larger opposite is actually the smaller value.
When performing __________, such as calculating (-1.5)+(-2.3)=-(1.5+2.3), we use sign rules to combine the numbers just like with integers.
__________ can always be rewritten as adding the opposite, following the rule a-b=a+(-b).
In __________, multiplying two values with the same sign, like (-2.5)(-4), always gives a positive result.
When doing __________ with different signs, such as (-4.8)0.2, the final quotient will always carry a minus sign.
__________ helps make long decimals simpler by dropping extra decimal digits or replacing integer digits with zeros to reach a specific place value.
According to the __________, if the digit immediately to the right of your target place is 5 or greater, you increase the target digit by 1; otherwise, you keep it the same.
When shopping at a supermarket and quickly checking if you have enough cash without calculating the exact cents, you are using __________ to find an approximate total.

title: Lesson 31: Some problems on ratios and percentages

exercises.text: Comparing 1 minute to 1 hour (60 minutes) gives a __________ of 1:60, which shows the quotient of two quantities measured in the same unit.
In everyday life, such as bank interest rates or store discounts, ratios are often written out of 100 as a __________.
When we divide 1 by 4 and multiply by 100, we write the result as 25% using the __________.
Finding a __________, like calculating 25% of 24, is done by multiplying 24 by 25100 to get 6.
A __________ of 1:10,000 tells us that 1cm measured on paper represents 10,000cm in the real world.

title: Lesson 32: Points and lines
wordBank: Point not lying on a line

exercises.text: A __________ is a basic geometric object that has position but no size, usually denoted by a capital letter like M or N.
A __________ extends infinitely in both directions without any bends, such as the line d shown in the figure.
In the first diagram, point M is a __________, meaning it lies directly on line d (written as Md).
Point N is a __________, meaning it sits outside of line d (written as Nd).
answers: point not lying on a line

exercises.text: When points A, C, and B all lie together on the same straight line, they are referred to as __________.
If point C does not lie on the line passing through A and B, then A, B, and C are called __________.
When two distinct lines cross each other, they are known as __________.
The single shared location where two crossing lines meet is called their __________.
Two distinct straight lines that never meet and have no shared points are called __________.
If two lines share two or more distinct points, they are considered to be __________ because they lie right on top of each other.

title: Lesson 33: Points between two points. Rays
wordBank: Two points on the same side of a point
Two points on opposite sides of a point

exercises.text: In the first diagram, point B is a __________, because it lies in between points A and C on the same straight line.
Looking at figure 8.11, points A and B are considered to be _________ relative to point C.
answers: two points on the same side of a point

exercises.text: Points A and C are referred to as __________ with respect to point B because they sit on opposite sides of B.
answers: two points on opposite sides of a point

exercises.text: A __________ consists of a starting point and extends infinitely in one direction along a line.
In ray Am, the starting point A is known as the __________ from which the ray begins.
When two rays share the exact same starting point and extend in the exact same direction, such as ray Am and ray AB, they are called __________.
Two rays that share a common origin and extend in opposite directions along the same straight line, like Ox and Oy, are known as __________.

title: Lesson 34: Line segments. Length of line segments

exercises.text: A __________ is a geometric figure consisting of two points A and B together with all the points lying between them.
In figure 8.15, the two boundary points A and B that mark the start and end of segment AB are called the __________.
Every segment has a specific measurement represented by a positive number, which is known as the __________.
The length of segment AB is also referred to as the __________, which equals 0 when the two points coincide.
__________ allows us to determine whether one segment is shorter than, longer than, or equal to another, such as writing AB<CD or AB=EG.
Before checking if a location divides a segment into equal halves, we must first verify that it is a __________ on the straight line.
When a point sits precisely in the middle, its distance to endpoint A is equal to its distance to endpoint B, making both endpoints __________ from that point.
The specific term for a point that lies between two endpoints and satisfies IA=IB is the __________.

title: Lesson 36: Angles
wordBank: Point in the interior of an angle

exercises.text: Two rays Ox and Oy sharing the same starting point form a geometric figure called an __________.
In figure 8.23, the common endpoint O where the two rays meet is known as the __________.
Looking at angle xOy, the two rays Ox and Oy are called the __________.
In figure 8.25, point M sits strictly between the two rays (not on the rays or outside like point N), so M is a __________.
answers: point in the interior of an angle

exercises.text: Every angle has a specific numeric __________ that tells how "wide" it opens, measured with units like degrees.
A straight angle has a measurement of 180°, where the tiny raised circle symbol represents a single __________.
To measure or draw angle xOy precisely in geometry, we use a semi-circular tool called a __________.
An angle that measures exactly 90° is known as a __________.
An angle whose measure is greater than 0° but less than 90° is called an __________.
A __________ is larger than a right angle but smaller than a straight angle, measuring between 90° and 180°.
When two opposite rays form a line, the resulting shape is a __________ with a measure of exactly 180°.
Information collected through observation, experiments, or surveys is broadly referred to as __________.
When information is expressed in numbers, such as weights, heights, or scores, it is classified as __________.
Information consisting of words, categories, or descriptions (like favorite colors or blood types) is known as __________.
Methods such as conducting questionnaires, making observations, or gathering information from existing sources are part of __________.
Checking whether collected figures make sense and identifying any unreasonable entries helps ensure the __________.
Organizing collected data into neat rows and columns creates a __________, making it easy to read and analyze the numbers.
Instead of writing only numbers, a __________ uses small pictures or icons to represent and display statistical data visually.
When reading a picture chart, we always look at the __________ to see how many items each single icon represents (for example, one apple icon = 10 apples).
A __________ uses rectangular bars of equal width to represent and compare different categories of data visually.
When setting up a standard column chart, the quantitative values are typically measured along the __________ running up and down.
The categories or groups being compared (such as months, classes, or names) are laid out along the __________ running left to right.
To compare two sets of data side-by-side for the same categories (such as comparing boys' and girls' sports preferences over two years), we use a __________.
When looking at a multi-series chart, we check the __________ to understand what each colored or patterned column represents.

title: Lesson 42: Possible outcomes and events in games and experiments

exercises.text: When we roll a die or toss a coin to observe its random behavior, the action itself is called an __________.
Each individual result that can possibly happen when performing a trial is known as a __________.
A specific condition or outcome that we check to see whether it occurs during a game or test is referred to as an __________.
When we repeat an experiment multiple times, the total count of how many times the test is performed is called the __________.
The number of times a specific event or outcome actually occurs during those tests is known as its __________.
By dividing the number of successful outcomes by the total number of attempts, we can calculate the __________, which shows how likely an event is based on practical tests.
